cards.title: Citizen Kane (1941)
cards.body: Deep focus, nonlinear structure, and subjective memory made this a blueprint for modern narrative cinema.

cards.title: Bicycle Thieves (1948)
cards.body: Italian neorealism shows systemic pressure through ordinary life, using location shooting and nonprofessional actors.

cards.title: Tokyo Story (1953)
cards.body: Ozu's still framing and restrained pacing turn small family moments into profound emotional distance.

cards.title: The 400 Blows (1959)
cards.body: French New Wave realism and handheld immediacy made adolescent interiority feel urgent and unscripted.

cards.title: The Godfather (1972)
cards.body: Power, ritual, and family loyalty are staged as legacy while moral boundaries collapse.

cards.title: Taxi Driver (1976)
cards.body: Urban alienation is framed through subjective paranoia, isolation, and identity fragmentation.

cards.title: In the Mood for Love (2000)
cards.body: Repetition, spatial restraint, and withheld desire create emotional intensity without explicit resolution.

cards.title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind (2004)
cards.body: Memory erasure becomes a study of attachment loops, grief, and unfinished emotional learning.

cards.title: Before Sunrise (1995)
cards.body: Dialogic intimacy turns conversation itself into plot, making emotional risk the central action.

cards.title: Do the Right Thing (1989)
cards.body: Escalation under heat and social pressure shows how unresolved tensions become civic rupture.

cards.title: Her (2013)
cards.body: A relationship with an evolving AI explores intimacy, dependency, growth, and asymmetry of change.

cards.title: Moonlight (2016)
cards.body: Identity formation is rendered through silence, gaze, and body language across life phases.

cards.title: Parasite (2019)
cards.body: Genre shifts and spatial design expose class aspiration, humiliation, and moral ambiguity.

cards.title: Aftersun (2022)
cards.body: Fragmentary memory and retrospective framing show how meaning changes as we mature.

cards.title: Renaissance Perspective
cards.body: Linear perspective organized pictorial space mathematically, aligning art with humanist inquiry.

cards.title: Leonardo's Sfumato
cards.body: Sfumato softens edges to model perception and psychological ambiguity rather than strict outline.

cards.title: Caravaggio's Tenebrism
cards.body: Extreme light-dark contrast directs emotional focus and moral drama into the body.

cards.title: Dutch Golden Age Genre Painting
cards.body: Domestic scenes encoded class, labor, and morality inside ordinary interiors.

cards.title: Impressionism
cards.body: Impressionists emphasized changing light and lived perception over polished academic finish.

cards.title: Post-Impressionist Structure
cards.body: Cezanne, Van Gogh, and Gauguin pushed color and form toward emotional and structural invention.

cards.title: Cubism
cards.body: Cubism fragmented single-point perspective to represent objects as simultaneous viewpoints.

cards.title: Dada and Anti-Art
cards.body: Dada used absurdity and readymades to reject war-era rationality and art market norms.

cards.title: Abstract Expressionism
cards.body: Gesture and scale in postwar painting reframed the canvas as event and existential arena.

cards.title: Conceptual Art
cards.body: Conceptual artists argued that idea and context can outrank material craft.

cards.title: Feminist Art Interventions
cards.body: Feminist practice exposed gendered exclusion in canon, labor, and authorship systems.

cards.title: Relational Aesthetics Debate
cards.body: Participation-based work raised questions about sociality, power, and who gets included.

cards.title: Plato on Forms
cards.body: Plato distinguishes unstable appearances from stable intelligible forms as objects of knowledge.

cards.title: Aristotle's Virtue Ethics
cards.body: Character is built by habituated practice aimed at flourishing in concrete situations.

cards.title: Stoic Control Dichotomy
cards.body: Stoicism trains attention toward what can be governed: judgment, intention, and response.

cards.title: Kantian Duty
cards.body: Moral action should be universalizable and grounded in respect for persons as ends.

cards.title: Utilitarian Reasoning
cards.body: Consequentialism evaluates action by aggregate well-being outcomes, with fairness challenges.

cards.title: Existential Responsibility
cards.body: Existentialism frames freedom as responsibility: choices define meaning under uncertainty.

cards.title: Phenomenology
cards.body: Phenomenology examines lived experience before abstract theory, emphasizing first-person structure.

cards.title: Pragmatism
cards.body: Pragmatism tests ideas by practical consequences and revisability in community.

cards.title: Care Ethics
cards.body: Care ethics centers relational interdependence, vulnerability, and situated responsibility.

cards.title: Hermeneutics
cards.body: Interpretation is historically situated; understanding evolves as context and perspective shift.

cards.title: Virtue Epistemology
cards.body: Good knowing depends on cultivated intellectual virtues like humility and rigor.

cards.title: Philosophy of Mind Basics
cards.body: Core debates ask how subjective experience relates to brain processes and identity.

cards.title: Deliberate Practice
cards.body: Break skills into subskills, train at challenge edge, and use rapid feedback loops.

cards.title: Spacing Effect
cards.body: Distributed review over time improves durable recall more than massed repetition.

cards.title: Retrieval Practice
cards.body: Testing yourself from memory strengthens access paths more than passive rereading.

cards.title: Interleaving
cards.body: Mixing related problem types increases discrimination and transfer despite short-term struggle.

cards.title: Desirable Difficulty
cards.body: Harder practice that remains solvable can improve long-term retention and adaptability.

cards.title: Metacognition
cards.body: Expert learners monitor confidence, calibrate errors, and adjust strategies intentionally.

cards.title: Habit Loop Design
cards.body: Reliable habits use clear cues, low-friction starts, and identity-consistent rewards.

cards.title: Transfer Across Domains
cards.body: Transfer improves when principles are abstracted, contrasted, and applied in varied contexts.

cards.title: Values Alignment
cards.body: Long-term compatibility depends more on shared values and conflict style than pure chemistry.

cards.title: Attachment Fit
cards.body: Compatibility improves when both partners can co-regulate stress without chronic protest-withdraw cycles.

cards.title: Communication Compatibility
cards.body: Predictability in repair language matters more than debate skill during conflict.

cards.title: Lifestyle and Timing
cards.body: Major mismatch in pace, priorities, or life stage can mimic emotional incompatibility.

cards.title: Boundaries and Reciprocity
cards.body: Healthy compatibility includes symmetrical respect for boundaries and effort.

cards.title: Green Flags as Behaviors
cards.body: Green flags are repeated actions: accountability, consistency, emotional availability, and repair.

cards.title: Chemistry vs Stability Tradeoff
cards.body: High intensity without stability can feel magnetic but is hard to sustain.

cards.title: Decision Rule for Compatibility
cards.body: Ask: can we be fully ourselves, handle stress well, and build trust faster than we damage it?

cards.title: Psychological Safety in Friendship
cards.body: Strong friendships permit vulnerability without punishment or scorekeeping.

cards.title: Bid for Connection
cards.body: Small bids for attention matter; consistent turning-toward predicts closeness.

cards.title: Repair After Rupture
cards.body: Repair needs owning impact, not just intent, plus a concrete behavior change.

cards.title: Reciprocity Over Time
cards.body: Reciprocity can vary short term but should balance over longer cycles.

cards.title: Boundaries Between Friends
cards.body: Boundaries protect trust; resentment often signals boundary drift rather than lack of care.

cards.title: Conflict Style Mismatch
cards.body: Pursuer-avoider patterns can misread each other as rejection versus pressure.

cards.title: Loyalty and Accountability
cards.body: Loyalty is not blind agreement; mature friendship allows truthful challenge.

cards.title: Friendship Drift
cards.body: Drift is often logistical before emotional; naming it early can prevent silent endings.

cards.title: Betrayal Injury
cards.body: Betrayal combines grief, identity shock, and threat to your map of reality.

cards.title: Deception and Nervous System
cards.body: After betrayal, hypervigilance is common because prediction safety has been broken.

cards.title: Trust Rebuilding Criteria
cards.body: Trust rebuild requires transparency, consistency, and tolerance for hard questions over time.

cards.title: Apology Quality
cards.body: Effective apologies include impact ownership, no minimization, and changed action.

cards.title: Forgiveness vs Reconciliation
cards.body: Forgiveness can be internal; reconciliation requires restored safety and boundaries.

cards.title: Repeat Lying Pattern
cards.body: Chronic lying erodes epistemic trust; relationship viability depends on behavior shift, not promises.

cards.title: Post-Betrayal Boundaries
cards.body: Boundary clarity after betrayal reduces rumination and supports agency.

cards.title: When to Exit
cards.body: If harm repeats without meaningful accountability, distance can be a healthy protective move.

cards.title: Affective vs Cognitive Empathy
cards.body: Affective empathy feels with someone; cognitive empathy understands their perspective.

cards.title: Accurate Reflection
cards.body: Good empathy reflects specific emotion and context, then checks if it landed.

cards.title: Validation Without Agreement
cards.body: Validation acknowledges internal reality; it does not require endorsing every action.

cards.title: Empathic Listening Sequence
cards.body: Mirror, clarify, then ask one open question. Do not jump to fixing too early.

cards.title: Compassion Fatigue
cards.body: Without boundaries, empathy can become depletion. Regulated care is more sustainable.

cards.title: Attunement Rupture
cards.body: Empathic misses are normal; quick repair protects connection more than perfection.

cards.title: High-Conflict Empathy
cards.body: In conflict, concise empathy plus a clear boundary prevents escalation and collapse.

cards.title: Empathy and Accountability
cards.body: Empathy should reduce shame while still preserving responsibility for behavior.

cards.title: Belonging Cues
cards.body: Belonging grows through repeated cues of welcome, responsiveness, and low social threat.

cards.title: Attachment Security
cards.body: Secure bonds balance closeness and autonomy while repairing rupture quickly.

cards.title: Co-Regulation
cards.body: Nervous systems influence each other; calm tone and pacing can downshift stress together.

cards.title: Loneliness Mechanics
cards.body: Loneliness is not only social quantity; it reflects unmet intimacy and recognition.

cards.title: Mutuality
cards.body: Healthy connection includes turn-taking in care, influence, and emotional labor.

cards.title: Relational Depth
cards.body: Depth increases with specificity, emotional risk, and reliable follow-through over time.

cards.title: Boundaries as Connection Tools
cards.body: Clear boundaries prevent hidden resentment and make closeness safer.

cards.title: Rupture and Repair Cycle
cards.body: Strong relationships are not rupture-free; they recover through fast, honest repair loops.

cards.title: Attachment Withdrawal Is Real
cards.body: Early heartbreak often feels chemically intense; treat it like nervous-system withdrawal and prioritize sleep, nutrition, movement, and social support before major decisions.

cards.title: No-Contact as Boundary Hygiene
cards.body: No-contact is not a game; it is a boundary that reduces re-triggering and helps your cognition return to baseline.

cards.title: Chemistry vs Compatibility
cards.body: Missing intensity does not prove compatibility. Evaluate consistency, honesty, emotional availability, and repair behavior over time.

cards.title: Closure Through Agency
cards.body: Closure is often built through action, not granted by an ex. Define one boundary, one self-respecting behavior, and one support ritual each day.
